@sansa\_grey Fair concern, and honestly the reason we built it the way we did.

Wisry doesn't copy the visuals. It reads the structure of the ad that's working: the hook, the pacing, where the proof lands, how it closes. Then it rebuilds that around your product, your footage or avatar, your palette, your script. Two brands cloning the same source ad end up with two different ads that share a skeleton.

The other thing is the research citation. You see which ads it drew from, so if everyone in your niche is running the same format, you can pick a different source, or have it fan out hook variants instead. [...] Amy Bradley

Does the system adjust the creative when the original winning ad targets a very different customer segment?

Ruta Jaskunaite

@amybradley Good question. Yes, partly by design and partly by you.

Wisry starts from your store, not the source ad. It reads your products and who you sell to first, and that brand profile is what the script, the avatar and the visuals get built against. So what carries over from the source ad is the structure (hook, pacing, proof, close), not the audience or the message. [...] That said, if you pick a source ad aimed at a totally different buyer, the skeleton might just not fit. That's why the research step ranks ads from your own market first. And if something's off, you don't re-edit by hand. You tell the agent in chat what to change, say "make this speak to first-time buyers, not repeat customers", and it rewrites that part while keeping everything else consistent: the script, the scene timing, the captions, the product claims. Is there a specific case you're thinking of?
